sentences.zh: 後漢書志第五 禮儀中 立夏請雨拜皇太子拜王公桃印黃郊立秋貙劉案戶祠星立冬

translations.literal: Book of Later Han, Treatise 5: Etiquette (middle): Beginning of Summer, praying for rain, investing the heir apparent, investing kings and dukes, peach talismans, the yellow suburban sacrifice, Beginning of Autumn, the autumn hunt (Chu Liu), inspecting doors, sacrificing to the stars, Beginning of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Treatise 5—Etiquette, part two: rites from Beginning of Summer through Beginning of Winter, including rain prayers, enthroning the crown prince, honoring nobles with imperial audience, peach charms, the yellow suburban offering, the autumn hunt, door inspections, star sacrifices, and seasonal commencements.

sentences.zh: 冬至臘大儺土牛遣衛士朝會立夏之日，夜漏未盡五刻，京都百官皆衣赤，至季夏衣黃，郊。

translations.literal: Winter solstice, year-end sacrifice (la), great exorcism (nuo), clay ox, dispatching guards, court assembly; on the day of Beginning of Summer, before the fifth mark of the night clepsydra has run out, all officials of the capital wear red; by the last month of summer they wear yellow, [for] the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter covers winter solstice, the la festival, the great nuo exorcism, the clay ox, rotating the guards, and the court gathering. On Beginning of Summer, while less than five night clepsydra marks remain before dawn, everyone in the capital bureaucracy wears red; through late summer they switch to yellow, then observe the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其禮：祠特，祭醋。

translations.literal: As for the ritual: they sacrifice a single victim (te), and perform the vinegar offering.
translations.idiomatic: The liturgy calls for a single beast and the vinegar libation.

sentences.zh: 自立春至立夏盡立秋，郡國上雨澤。

translations.literal: From Beginning of Spring through Beginning of Summer until Beginning of Autumn ends, the commanderies and kingdoms submit reports on rainfall.
translations.idiomatic: Between Beginning of Spring and the close of Beginning of Autumn, every commandery and kingdom forwards rainfall records to the court.

sentences.zh: 其旱也，公卿官長以次行雩禮求雨。

translations.literal: When there is drought, dukes, ministers, and officials in rank order perform the yu rite to seek rain.
translations.idiomatic: In time of drought, senior ministers and local magistrates take turns performing the Great Yu ceremony to pray for rain.

sentences.zh: [一]閉諸陽，衣皁，興土龍，[二]立土人舞僮二佾，七日一變如故事。

translations.literal: [One] Close off all yang [omens]; wear black clothing; erect clay dragons; [two] set up clay figures and boy dancers in two rows (yi); once every seven days change [the arrangement] according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: First, seal every yang portal, dress in black, and raise earthen dragons; second, station clay effigies and two ranks of boy dancers, altering the setup every seven days as statute prescribes.

sentences.zh: [三]反拘朱索*[縈]*社，伐朱鼓。

translations.literal: [Three] Invert [the cord], bind red cords *[coiling]* around the she altar, and strike the red drum.
translations.idiomatic: Third, reverse the bindings, loop red cords around the soil altar, and beat the crimson drum.

sentences.zh: [四]禱賽以少牢如禮。

translations.literal: [Four] Pray and give thanks with a lesser sacrifice (shao lao) according to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, offer prayer and votive thanks with a pig-and-goat set, following canonical form.

sentences.zh: [五] 注[一]公羊傳曰：「大雩，旱祭也。

translations.literal: [Five] Comment [one]: The Gongyang Commentary says, "The great yu is the drought sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary note 1: The Gongyang Commentary calls the great yu the ceremony held against drought.

sentences.zh: 」何休注曰：「君親之南郊，以六事謝過自責曰：『政不善與？

translations.literal: " He Xiu's commentary says: "The ruler personally [goes] to the southern suburb and, with six topics, apologizes for faults and reproaches himself, saying: 'Is governance not good?
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu explains that the sovereign himself travels to the southern suburban altar and enumerates six faults, asking in ritual self-reproach: Is my rule unjust?

sentences.zh: 民失職與？

translations.literal: Have the people lost their proper livelihood?
translations.idiomatic: Have the people been robbed of their occupations?

sentences.zh: 宮室崇與？

translations.literal: Are palaces and chambers excessive?
translations.idiomatic: Have my halls grown wastefully grand?

sentences.zh: 婦謁盛與？

translations.literal: Is women's lobbying abundant?
translations.idiomatic: Has influence peddling through the women's quarters run rampant?

sentences.zh: 苞苴行與？

translations.literal: Do wrapped bribes circulate?
translations.idiomatic: Are gifts and bribes changing hands?

sentences.zh: 讒夫倡與？

translations.literal: Do slanderous men lead the way?
translations.idiomatic: Are deceivers setting the tone at court?

translations.literal: '" He causes boys and girls, eight of each, to dance and cry "yu"; therefore it is called yu.
translations.idiomatic: He then has eight boys and eight girls dance and chant the yu cry—hence the name of the rite.

sentences.zh: 」春秋繁露曰：「大旱雩祭而請雨，大水鳴鼓而攻社，天地之所為，陰陽之所起也。

translations.literal: " The Chunqiu Fanlu says: "In great drought one performs the yu sacrifice and prays for rain; in great flood one beats drums and attacks the she altar—this is what Heaven and Earth do, where yin and yang arise."
translations.idiomatic: The Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals adds that severe drought calls for the yu offering to plead for rain, whereas inundation calls for drumming against the soil altar—each response follows what Heaven and Earth authorize through shifting yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 曰：大旱，陽滅陰也。

translations.literal: It is said: Great drought means yang extinguishes yin.
translations.idiomatic: The answer runs: a killing drought means dominant yang has smothered yin.

sentences.zh: 陽滅陰者，尊厭卑也。

translations.literal: When yang extinguishes yin, the noble presses down the base.
translations.idiomatic: When yang prevails absolutely, the high naturally weighs upon the low.

sentences.zh: 固其義也，雖大甚，拜請之而已，敢有加也？

translations.literal: Solid is its propriety; though [the imbalance] be extreme, one bows and requests—that is all—how dare one add [violence]?
translations.idiomatic: That propriety holds firm: even in extreme drought one only bows and begs—who would dare escalate to coercion?

sentences.zh: 大水者，陰滅陽也。

translations.literal: Great flood means yin extinguishes yang.
translations.idiomatic: Catastrophic flooding means yin has overwhelmed yang.

sentences.zh: 陰滅陽者，卑勝尊也。

translations.literal: When yin extinguishes yang, the base conquers the noble.
translations.idiomatic: When yin surges, the lowly briefly overturn the lofty.

sentences.zh: 以賤陵貴者逆節，故鳴鼓而攻之，朱絲而脅之，為其不義，此亦春秋之不畏強禦也。

translations.literal: For the mean to overawe the noble is contrary to proper order; therefore one beats drums and attacks it, binds it with red silk and constrains it—because it is unjust; this too is the Spring and Autumn Annals' fearlessness toward the mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Inferiors lording over superiors inverts the cosmic hierarchy, so drummers assault the altar, red cords truss it up, and public shame punishes injustice—the Annals likewise sanction defiance of brute force.

sentences.zh: 又仲舒奏江都王云：「求雨之方，損陽益陰。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhongshu memorialized the Prince of Jiangdu, saying: "The method of seeking rain is to diminish yang and augment yin.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu likewise advised the Prince of Jiangdu that rain magic weakens yang and nourishes yin.

sentences.zh: 願大王無收廣陵女子為人祝者一月租，賜諸巫者；

translations.literal: I beg Your Greatness not to collect the one-month rent from Guangling women who serve as invocators; grant it to the various shamans;
translations.idiomatic: He urged the prince to remit one month's levy on Guangling women hired as prayer leaders and to divert that sum to the temple shamans;

sentences.zh: 諸巫毋大小皆相聚於郭門，為小壇，以脯酒祭；

translations.literal: let all shamans, great and small, assemble together at the outer gate, make a small altar, and sacrifice with dried meat and ale;
translations.idiomatic: have every shaman, junior or senior, gather outside the city wall, raise a modest earthen altar, and offer meat and wine;

sentences.zh: 女獨擇寬大便處移巿，巿便無內丈夫，丈夫無得相從飲食；

translations.literal: women alone select a spacious, convenient place and shift the market; in the market convenience no husbands may enter; husbands may not follow one another in eating and drinking;
translations.idiomatic: let women choose an open, convenient site for a provisional market from which all males are barred so husbands cannot trail their wives to meals;

sentences.zh: 令吏妻各往視其夫，皆到即起，雨注而已。

translations.literal: order the wives of clerks each to go observe their husbands; when all have arrived,then rise—rain will pour down and stop.
translations.idiomatic: then dispatch clerks' wives to visit their husbands' posts; the moment every wife has appeared, the clouds burst and the drought ends.

sentences.zh: 」服虔注左傳曰：「大雩，夏祭天名。

translations.literal: " Fu Qian's commentary on the Zuo Tradition says: "The great yu is the name of the summer sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian's Zuo commentary defines the great yu as the midsummer sacrifice addressed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 雩，遠也，遠為百谷求膏雨也。

translations.literal: Yu means 'distant'; distantly [Heaven] seeks enriching rain for the hundred grains."
translations.idiomatic: The word yu implies reaching far abroad to beg Heaven's soaking rains for every crop in the field.

sentences.zh: 龍見而雩。

translations.literal: When the Dragon [asterism] appears, then one performs the yu.
translations.idiomatic: The canon prescribes the yu as soon as the Dragon constellation rises.

sentences.zh: 龍，角、亢也。

translations.literal: The Dragon: [its first stars are] Horn and Neck [Jiao and Kang].
translations.idiomatic: Here "Dragon" denotes the Horn and Neck lunar lodges.

sentences.zh: 謂四月□，龍星體見，萬物始盛，待雨而大，故雩祭以求雨也。

translations.literal: It means in the fourth month [lacuna], the dragon stars appear in full; the myriad things have begun to flourish; they await rain to grow great; therefore the yu sacrifice is performed to seek rain.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month—where the text is damaged—the dragon asterism stands fully above the horizon, growth has begun in earnest, and every plant waits on timely rain, which is why the court stages the yu.

sentences.zh: 」一說，大雩者，祭於帝而祈雨也。

translations.literal: " One explanation: the great yu sacrifices to the [Supreme] Emperor and prays for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss treats the great yu as a petition for rain offered directly to the high god.

sentences.zh: 一說，郊，祀天祈農事；

translations.literal: One explanation: the suburban sacrifice worships Heaven and prays for agricultural work;
translations.idiomatic: Still others distinguish the suburban rite, which entreats Heaven on behalf of farming,

sentences.zh: 雩，祭山川而祈雨也。

translations.literal: the yu sacrifices to mountains and rivers and prays for rain.
translations.idiomatic: from the yu, which beseeches mountains and rivers for showers.

sentences.zh: 漢舊儀：「求雨，太常禱天地、宗廟、社稷、山川以賽，各如其常牢，禮也。

translations.literal: Han Old Observances: "When seeking rain, the Chamberlain for Ceremonies prays to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, soil and grain altars, and mountains and rivers with thank-offerings; each according to its usual victim—this is proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Han Old Observances, rain prayers require the Minister of Ceremonies to offer stipulated victims at Heaven and Earth, the imperial shrines, she and ji, and watercourses—each venue receiving its ordinary livestock complement.

sentences.zh: 四月立夏旱，乃求雨禱雨而已；

translations.literal: If in the fourth month, at Beginning of Summer, there is drought, then one seeks rain and prays for rain—that is all;
translations.idiomatic: When drought strikes at the fourth-month Beginning of Summer, only the statutory rain entreaties are performed;

sentences.zh: 後旱，復重禱而已；

translations.literal: if afterward there is drought again, again double the prayers—that is all;
translations.idiomatic: should dryness return later, the court simply repeats the layered prayers;

sentences.zh: 訖立秋，雖旱不得禱求雨也。」

translations.literal: throughout down to Beginning of Autumn, though there be drought, one may not pray to seek rain."
translations.idiomatic: but after Beginning of Autumn, even severe drought does not justify further rain magic.

sentences.zh: 注[二]山海經曰：「大荒東北隅有山，名曰凶廣土丘。

translations.literal: Comment [two]: The Classic of Mountains and Seas says: "In the northeast corner of the Great Wilds there is a mountain called Ferocious-vast Earth-mound (Xiongguang Tuqiu).
translations.idiomatic: Comment 2 quotes the Classic of Mountains and Seas: northeast of the Great Wasteland rises Mount Xiongguangtuqiu.

sentences.zh: 應龍處南極，殺蚩尤與誇父，不得復上，故下數旱。

translations.literal: The responding dragon (ying long) dwells at the south pole; it killed Chiyou and Kuafu, and could not ascend again; therefore below there are frequent droughts.
translations.idiomatic: The responsive dragon guards the southern pole; after slaying Chiyou and Kuafu it can no longer soar skyward, so the human realm suffers repeated drought.

sentences.zh: 旱而為應龍之狀，乃得大雨。

translations.literal: When there is drought, [if] one forms the shape of the responding dragon, then one obtains great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Fashioning an effigy of that dragon during drought draws down the deluge.

sentences.zh: 」郭璞曰：「今之土龍，本此氣應，自然冥感，非人所能為也。

translations.literal: " Guo Pu says: "Today's clay dragons take their sympathetic resonance from this; it is a dark natural sympathy—nothing humans contrive."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu adds that modern clay dragons echo this primordial resonance with qi—a spontaneous sympathy beyond human craft.

sentences.zh: 」董仲舒云：「春旱求雨，令縣邑以水日令民禱社稷，家人祠戶。

translations.literal: " Dong Zhongshu says: "When spring drought seeks rain, order the counties and towns on water days to have the people pray to the she and ji altars; households sacrifice to the door [spirits].
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu prescribes spring drought rituals: on designated water-phase days every county prays at the soil and grain shrines while families sacrifice to their gate gods.

sentences.zh: 毋伐名木，毋斬山林。

translations.literal: Do not cut famous trees; do not hew mountain forests.
translations.idiomatic: Logging famed timber or clearing upland woods is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 暴巫聚蛇八日。

translations.literal: Expose the witches and gather snakes for eight days.
translations.idiomatic: For eight days shamans sun themselves in the open while snakes are assembled—per Dong Zhongshu's liturgy.

sentences.zh: 於邑東門之外為四通之壇，方八尺，植蒼繒八。

translations.literal: Outside the east gate of the town make a four-way altar, eight feet square, and plant eight bolts of grey silk.
translations.idiomatic: East of the town gate workers raise an eight-foot-square crossroads altar hung with eight panels of gray silk.

sentences.zh: 其神共工。

translations.literal: Its spirit is Gonggong.
translations.idiomatic: Gonggong presides over that altar.

translations.literal: Select among the shamans those who are pure, clean, eloquent of mouth and sharp of phrase to serve as invocator.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the cleanest, most articulate medium to intone the prayer.

sentences.zh: 祝齋三日，服蒼衣。

translations.literal: The invocator fasts three days and wears grey-green clothing.
translations.idiomatic: That officiant fasts three days and dresses in ash-colored robes.

sentences.zh: 先再拜，乃跪陳，陳已，復再拜，乃起。

translations.literal: First twice bow; then kneel and declaim; when the declamation is finished, again twice bow; then rise.
translations.idiomatic: He bows twice, kneels to recite the petition, bows twice again, and only then stands.

translations.literal: The invocator says: 'August Heaven produced the five grains to nourish mankind.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer begins: “High Heaven grew the five cereals to feed us.”

sentences.zh: 今五穀病旱，恐不成。

translations.literal: Now the five grains are sick with drought; I fear they will not mature.
translations.idiomatic: “Now drought blights those crops; they may never ripen.”

translations.literal: If by fortune rain heavily soaks [the earth], present victims and pray thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Should Heaven answer with a soaking shower, they immediately offer livestock in gratitude.

translations.idiomatic: On Wood-day jia and yi they mold one immense blue dragon, eight zhang in length, at the center;

translations.literal: make seven small dragons, each four zhang long, in the east; all face east; the space between each is eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: seven lesser dragons, each four zhang, line up to the east, snouts eastward, eight chi apart.

translations.literal: Eight young boys, all fast three days, wear green clothing and dance them.
translations.idiomatic: Eight acolytes, fasting three days in green coats, dance around those effigies.

translations.literal: The field overseer (tian se fu) also fasts three days, wears green clothing, and stands them up.
translations.idiomatic: The hamlet field warden likewise fasts, dons green, and supervises the setup.

translations.idiomatic: They cut channels from the she altar to the moat beyond the ward gate.

translations.idiomatic: Five wicker fish traps are staggered across the soil-altar court.

translations.literal: The invocator fasts three days, wears grey-green clothing, bows, kneels, and declaims the prayer as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The invocator repeats the three-day fast, gray robes, and original choreography.

sentences.zh: 取三歲雄雞與三歲豭豬，皆燔之於四通神宇。

translations.literal: Take three-year-old cocks and three-year-old boars; all roast them at the four-way spirit enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Three-year roosters and boars burn at the crossroads shrine.

sentences.zh: 令民闔邑裡南門，置水其外，開裡北門。

translations.literal: Order the people to shut the south gate of the town and ward, place water outside it, and open the north gate of the ward.
translations.idiomatic: Residents seal the town's south gate, heap water outside, and open the northern lane gate.

sentences.zh: 具老豭豬一，置之裡北門之外。

translations.literal: Prepare one old boar; place it outside the north gate of the ward.
translations.idiomatic: An old boar waits beyond the lane's north exit.

sentences.zh: 巿中亦置一豭豬。

translations.literal: In the market also place one boar.
translations.idiomatic: A second boar stands in the marketplace.

translations.idiomatic: the drum signal, they singe every pig's tail, bury bones taken from old graves, unblock mountain springs, and heap fuel for bonfires.

sentences.zh: 決信道橋之壅塞不行者決瀆之。

translations.literal: Decide: where irrigation channels and bridges are blocked and impassable, open the ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Every clogged canal or bridge fairway is dredged until water moves freely.

sentences.zh: 幸而得雨，報以豚一，酒、鹽、黍財足。

translations.literal: If fortunately rain is obtained, give thanks with one suckling pig; ale, salt, and millet as wealth suffices.
translations.idiomatic: When rain finally falls, the thank-offering is a single piglet plus ale, salt, and whatever millet the town can spare.

sentences.zh: 以茅為席，毋斷。

translations.literal: Use thatch for mats; do not cut [them] through.
translations.idiomatic: Rush mats must stay whole—never slash them apart.

sentences.zh: 夏求雨，令縣邑以水日家人祀醋，毋舉土功。

translations.literal: In summer seeking rain, order the counties and towns on water days that households sacrifice the vinegar offering; do not undertake earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Summer drought protocol assigns water-phase days for domestic vinegar libations and forbids construction projects.

sentences.zh: 更大浚井。

translations.literal: Further greatly dredge the wells.
translations.idiomatic: They deepen and scour every well.

sentences.zh: 暴釜於壇，杵臼於術，七日。

translations.literal: Expose cauldrons on the altar; pestles and mortars on the road; seven days.
translations.idiomatic: For a week they sun cauldrons on the altar and set mortars in the lanes—another summer drought measure.

sentences.zh: 為四通之壇於邑南門之外，方七尺，植赤繒七。

translations.literal: They make a four-way altar outside the south gate of the town, seven chi square, and set up seven bolts of red silk.
translations.idiomatic: South of the town gate they build a crossroads altar seven chi on a side and hang seven panels of crimson silk.

sentences.zh: 其神蚩尤。

translations.literal: Its spirit is Chiyou.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou is the tutelary spirit of that stage.

sentences.zh: 祭之以赤雄雞七，玄酒，具清酒*

translations.literal: They sacrifice to it with seven red cocks, dark ale, and prepare clear ale *
translations.idiomatic: The offering includes seven crimson cocks, black millet wine, and clear ale

translations.literal: (variant character 搏 'pound').
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 搏 (pound, as in pounded meat).

translations.literal: **[dried shoulder]* meat.
translations.idiomatic: with dried shoulder jerky to complete the set.

sentences.zh: 祝齋三日，服赤衣，拜跪、陳祝如春。

translations.literal: The invocator fasts three days, wears red clothing, and bows, kneels, and declaims the prayer as in spring.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer leader fasts for three days, dons red, and follows the same bowing and recitation used in the spring rite.

sentences.zh: 以丙、丁日為赤大龍一，長七丈，居中；

translations.literal: On bing and ding days they make one great red dragon, seven zhang long, occupying the center;
translations.idiomatic: On Fire-day bing and ding they mold one great scarlet dragon, seven zhang long, for the center;

sentences.zh: 又為小龍六，*[各]*長三丈五尺，於南方，皆南鄉，其閒相去七尺。

translations.literal: They also make six small dragons, *[each]* three zhang and five chi long, in the south; all face south; the space between them is seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: six smaller dragons, each three and a half zhang, stand to the south, all snouts southward, seven chi apart.

sentences.zh: 壯者七人，皆齋三日，服赤衣而舞之。

translations.literal: Seven strong men, all fast three days, wear red clothing, and dance them.
translations.idiomatic: Seven able-bodied men, each fasting three days in red, dance the dragon effigies.

sentences.zh: 司空嗇夫亦齋三日，服赤衣而立之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works' field overseer (sikong se fu) also fasts three days, wears red clothing, and stands them up.
translations.idiomatic: The district overseer for public works likewise fasts, dresses in red, and supervises the array.

sentences.zh: 鑿社而通之閭外之溝。

translations.literal: They bore through the she [altar] and connect it to the ditch outside the ward gate.
translations.idiomatic: They open a channel from the soil altar to the moat beyond the ward.

sentences.zh: 取五蝦罶，錯置社之中。

translations.literal: They take five shrimp-weirs and interlace-place them within the she.
translations.idiomatic: Five fish traps are staggered across the inner court of the she altar.

sentences.zh: 池方七尺，深一尺。

translations.literal: The pool is seven chi square, one chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The basin measures seven chi square and one chi deep.

sentences.zh: 酒脯祭。

translations.literal: They sacrifice with ale and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: They offer wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 齋衣赤，拜跪、陳祝如初。

translations.literal: Fasting, they clothe in red, bow, kneel, and declaim the prayer as at first.
translations.idiomatic: After fasting in red vestments, they repeat the initial bows, kneelings, and prayer.

sentences.zh: 取三歲雄雞、豭豬，燔之四通神宇。

translations.literal: They take three-year-old cocks and boars; they roast them at the four-way spirit enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: They burn three-year roosters and boars at the crossroads shrine.

sentences.zh: 開陰閉陽如春也。

translations.literal: Open yin, close yang, as in spring.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pathways open while yang is sealed, exactly as in the spring protocol.

sentences.zh: 季夏，禱山陵以助之。

translations.literal: In the last month of summer, they pray to mountain tumuli to assist it.
translations.idiomatic: During late summer they add prayers at the imperial tumuli for extra efficacy.

sentences.zh: 令縣邑一徙巿於邑南門之外，五日，禁男子無得行入巿。

translations.literal: They order the county and town jointly to shift the market outside the south gate of the town; for five days they forbid men from being allowed to walk into the market.
translations.idiomatic: Every county relocates its market south of the wall for five days and bars men from entering it.

sentences.zh: 家人祠中溜。

translations.literal: Households sacrifice to the central rain gutter (zhong liu).
translations.idiomatic: Families offer domestic sacrifice at the central eaves runnel.

sentences.zh: 毋舉土功。

translations.literal: Do not undertake earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Excavation and building projects are suspended.

sentences.zh: 聚巫巿旁，為之結蓋。

translations.literal: They gather shamans beside the market and for them tie a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans assemble beside the market under a tied canopy.

sentences.zh: 為四通之壇於中央，植黃繒五。

translations.literal: They make a four-way altar in the center and plant five bolts of yellow silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the hub they raise another crossroads altar hung with five bolts of yellow silk.

sentences.zh: 其神後稷。

translations.literal: Its spirit is Houji.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Millet presides there.

translations.idiomatic: Some editions read the negative particle 毋.

sentences.zh: 令各為祝齋三日，衣黃衣，皆如春祠。

translations.literal: They order each to become invocator, fast three days, wear yellow clothing—all as in the spring sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Each officiant fasts three days in yellow robes, matching the spring liturgy.

sentences.zh: 以戊、己日為大黃龍一，長五丈，居中央；

translations.literal: On wu and ji days they make one great yellow dragon, five zhang long, occupying the center;
translations.idiomatic: On Earth-day wu and ji they set one five-zhang golden dragon at the center;

sentences.zh: 又為小龍四，各長二丈五尺，於中央，皆南鄉，其閒相去五尺。

translations.literal: They also make four small dragons, each two zhang and five chi long, in the center; all face south; the space between them is five chi.
translations.idiomatic: four smaller dragons, each two and a half zhang, ring that center facing south, five chi apart.

sentences.zh: 丈夫五人，皆齋三日，服黃衣而舞之。

translations.literal: Five husbands, all fast three days, wear yellow clothing, and dance them.
translations.idiomatic: Five adult men, fasting three days in saffron coats, dance the effigies.

sentences.zh: 老者亦齋三日，衣黃衣而立之。

translations.literal: Old men also fast three days, wear yellow clothing, and stand them up.
translations.idiomatic: Elders likewise fast, wear yellow, and oversee the formation.

sentences.zh: 亦通社中於閭外溝。

translations.literal: Also connect the interior of the she to the ditch outside the ward.
translations.idiomatic: Channels again link the she court to the outer ditch.

sentences.zh: 蝦罶池方五尺，深一尺。

translations.literal: The shrimp-weir pool is five chi square, one chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The trap basin is five chi square and one chi deep.

sentences.zh: 他皆如前。

translations.literal: All else is as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else follows the earlier instructions.

sentences.zh: 秋，暴巫□至九日。

translations.literal: In autumn, they expose the shamans [lacuna] up to nine days.
translations.idiomatic: For autumn the shamans remain exposed in the sun for as many as nine days—the lacuna marks damaged text in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 毋舉火事，煎金器。

translations.literal: Do not undertake fire affairs; boil metal vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Open flame work is banned; even heating bronze vessels counts as an offense against the rite.

sentences.zh: 家人祠門。

translations.literal: Households sacrifice to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Families sacrifice at their gates.

sentences.zh: 為四通之壇於邑西門之外，方九尺，植白繒九。

translations.literal: They make a four-way altar outside the west gate of the town, nine chi square, and plant nine bolts of white silk.
translations.idiomatic: West of the town wall stands a nine-chi crossroads altar draped with nine panels of white silk.

sentences.zh: 其神*

translations.literal: Its spirit *
translations.idiomatic: The presiding spirit is

translations.idiomatic: The compound begins with 太 (great).

translations.literal: **[Lesser]* Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao, the Lesser Brilliant sovereign.

sentences.zh: 祭之桐木魚九，玄酒，具清酒*

translations.literal: They sacrifice to it with nine paulownia-wood fish, dark ale, and prepare clear ale *
translations.idiomatic: They bring nine wooden fish carved from paulownia, black millet wine, and clear ale

translations.idiomatic: Variant 搏.

translations.idiomatic: with dried shoulder jerky.

sentences.zh: 衣白衣。

translations.literal: They clothe in white clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Participants wear white.

sentences.zh: 他如春。

translations.literal: The rest is like spring.
translations.idiomatic: Other steps mirror the spring ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以庚、辛日為大白龍一，長九丈，居中央；

translations.literal: On geng and xin days they make one great white dragon, nine zhang long, occupying the center;
translations.idiomatic: On Metal-day geng and xin they mold one nine-zhang white dragon at the center;

sentences.zh: 為小龍八，各長四丈五尺，於西方，皆西鄉，其閒相去九尺。

translations.literal: They make eight small dragons, each four zhang and five chi long, in the west; all face west; the space between them is nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: eight lesser dragons, each four and a half zhang, line the western quadrant facing west, nine chi apart.

sentences.zh: □者九人，皆齋三日，服白衣而舞之。

translations.literal: [Lacuna] persons, nine in number, all fast three days, wear white clothing, and dance them.
translations.idiomatic: Nine dancers—the title is lost in the lacuna—fast three days in white and animate the effigies.

sentences.zh: 司馬亦齋三日，衣白衣而立之，蝦罶池方九尺，深一尺。

translations.literal: The Minister of War (Sima) also fasts three days, wears white clothing, and stands them up; the shrimp-weir pool is nine chi square, one chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The military intendant fasts, dresses in white, and directs the array while the fish-trap pool spans nine chi square and one chi deep.

sentences.zh: 他如前。

translations.literal: The rest is as before.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining details repeat the prior pattern.

sentences.zh: 冬，舞龍六日，禱於名山以助之。

translations.literal: In winter, they dance the dragons six days; they pray at famous mountains to assist it.
translations.idiomatic: Winter adds six days of dragon dancing and prayers at celebrated peaks.

sentences.zh: 家人祠井。

translations.literal: Households sacrifice to the well.
translations.idiomatic: Families sacrifice at their wells.

sentences.zh: 毋壅水。

translations.literal: Do not block water.
translations.idiomatic: Damming streams or cisterns is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 為四通之壇於邑北門之外，方六尺，植黑繒六。

translations.literal: They make a four-way altar outside the north gate of the town, six chi square, and plant six bolts of black silk.
translations.idiomatic: North of the wall they build a six-chi crossroads altar hung with six bolts of black silk.

sentences.zh: 其神玄冥。

translations.literal: Its spirit is Xuanming.
translations.idiomatic: The black god Xuanming receives the offering.

sentences.zh: 祭之以黑狗子六，玄酒，具清酒*

translations.literal: They sacrifice to it with six black dogs, dark ale, and prepare clear ale *
translations.idiomatic: They offer six black puppies, black millet wine, and clear ale

translations.literal: (reads 搏).
translations.idiomatic: Variant 搏.

translations.literal: **[dried shoulder]* meat.
translations.idiomatic: with dried shoulder jerky.

sentences.zh: 祝齋三日，衣玄衣。

translations.literal: The invocator fasts three days and clothes in dark clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer leader fasts three days in deep black robes.

sentences.zh: 祝禮如春。

translations.literal: The invocator's ritual is like spring.
translations.idiomatic: His choreography follows the spring model.

sentences.zh: 以壬、癸日為大黑龍一，長六丈，居中央；

translations.literal: On ren and gui days they make one great black dragon, six zhang long, occupying the center;
translations.idiomatic: On Water-day ren and gui they raise one six-zhang black dragon at the hub;

sentences.zh: 又為小龍五，各長三丈，於北方，皆北鄉，其閒相去六尺。

translations.literal: They also make five small dragons, each three zhang long, in the north; all face north; the space between them is six chi.
translations.idiomatic: five smaller dragons, each three zhang, stand to the north, snouts northward, six chi apart.

sentences.zh: 老者六人，皆齋三日，衣黑衣而舞之。

translations.literal: Six old men, all fast three days, wear black clothing, and dance them.
translations.idiomatic: Six elders, fasting three days in black, dance the dragons.

sentences.zh: 尉亦齋三日，服黑衣而立之。

translations.literal: The commandant (wei) also fasts three days, wears black clothing, and stands them up.
translations.idiomatic: The district captain likewise fasts in black and directs the scene.

sentences.zh: 蝦罶池皆如春。

translations.literal: The shrimp-weir pools are all like spring.
translations.idiomatic: The fish-trap pools match the spring measurements.

sentences.zh: 四時皆庚子日，令吏民夫婦皆偶處。

translations.literal: In all four seasons, on gengzi days, they order clerks and commoners, husbands and wives, all to dwell in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Every seasonal suite assigns gengzi days on which officials and townsfolk keep conjugal privacy.

sentences.zh: 凡求雨，大體丈夫欲藏而居，女子欲和而樂。

translations.literal: In general when seeking rain, the overall pattern is that husbands wish to hide and dwell [within]; women wish to be harmonious and joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Rain magic generally keeps men indoors and encourages tranquil, joyful harmony among women.

translations.literal: " The responding dragon has wings.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary adds that the responsive dragon bears wings.

sentences.zh: 法言曰：「象龍之致雨。

translations.literal: The Model Sayings says: "Imitating the dragon brings rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong's Model Sayings remarks that mimicking the dragon summons rain.

sentences.zh: 艱矣哉，龍乎！

translations.literal: Difficult indeed, O dragon!
translations.idiomatic: How arduous it is to play the dragon!

sentences.zh: 龍乎！

translations.literal: O dragon!
translations.idiomatic: O dragon!

translations.literal: " The New Discourses says: "When Liu Xin brought down rain, he fully constructed clay dragons, blew pitch-pipes, and for the various techniques of the masters, there was none he did not completely set up.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan's New Discourses records Liu Xin's rain ritual: clay dragons, pitch-pipes, and every occult technique he could assemble.

sentences.zh: 譚問：『求雨所以為土龍，何也？

translations.literal: Tan asked: 'For seeking rain, the reason one makes clay dragons—what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan asks why clay dragons are fashioned when praying for rain.

translations.literal: ' It was said: 'When the dragon appears, then wind and rain arise to welcome and send it off; therefore according to its image and kind they make it.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: wherever dragons appear, wind and rain gather to escort them; effigies imitate that likeness.

translations.idiomatic: Comment 3 cites the Rites of Zhou: the lacuna probably named the Huang dance, performed against drought.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：「□，赤皁染羽為之也。」

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan says: "[Lacuna], it is made by dyeing feathers with red-black."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses the lost graph: feathers dyed russet and black—likely the Huang dancers' regalia.

sentences.zh: 旱歎，註：「陽也，用假色者，欲其有時而去之。」

translations.literal: Drought lament—annotation: "It is yang; using borrowed colors, they desire that [the drought] have its season and depart."
translations.idiomatic: The sigh against drought is glossed as yang symbolism: borrowed colors mark the drought as temporary.

sentences.zh: 注[四]漢舊儀曰：「成帝三年六月，始命諸官止雨，朱繩反縈社，擊鼓攻之，是後水旱常不和。

translations.idiomatic: Comment 4 quotes Han Old Observances: in Chengdi's third year the court first commanded anti-rain rituals—red cords reversed on the she altar and drum assaults—after which flood and drought rarely balanced.

translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao explains the red silk binding the soil altar.

translations.literal: The she is Supreme Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The she altar embodies great yin.

sentences.zh: 朱，火色也。

translations.literal: Red is the color of fire.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion belongs to the fire phase.

sentences.zh: 天子伐鼓於社，責腢陰也；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven beats drums at the she, reproaching yin;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drums at the she to reproach excessive yin;

sentences.zh: 諸侯用幣於社，請上公也；

translations.literal: feudal lords use silks at the she, requesting the high duke;
translations.idiomatic: nobles present silk offerings to summon the high lord of yin;

sentences.zh: 伐鼓於朝，退自攻也。

translations.literal: they beat drums at court, retreating to attack themselves.
translations.idiomatic: court drums turn blame inward on the ruler himself.

sentences.zh: 此聖人之厭勝之法也。」

translations.literal: This is the method of the sages for overwhelming [ill omens]."
translations.idiomatic: Such is the sage-kings' pattern for counter-magic against calamity.

sentences.zh: 注[五]漢書儀曰：「武帝元封日到七月畢賽之，秋冬春不求雨。

translations.literal: Comment [five]: Han Book Observances says: "From Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng day until the seventh month finish the thank-offering; in autumn, winter, and spring they do not seek rain.
translations.idiomatic: Comment 5 cites Han Book Observances: Wudi's Yuanfeng schedule ends rain prayers by the seventh month; autumn through spring forbids further entreaties.

sentences.zh: 」古今注曰：「武帝元封六年五月旱，女及巫丈夫不入市也。」

translations.literal: " The Ancient and Modern Notes says: "In the fifth month of Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng sixth year, during drought, women and shaman husbands did not enter the market."
translations.idiomatic: The Ancient and Modern Notes adds that during Wudi's sixth-year drought, women and male shamans avoided the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 拜皇太子之儀：百官會，位定，謁者引皇太子當御坐殿下，北面；

translations.literal: The ritual for investing the heir apparent: the hundred officials assemble; when positions are fixed, the herald leads the heir apparent opposite the imperial seat below the hall, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for enthroning the crown prince: once the court ranks settle, the herald stations the heir below the throne dais, facing north;

sentences.zh: 司空當太子西北，東面立。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works stands northwest of the heir apparent, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of Works stations himself northwest of the prince, facing east.

sentences.zh: 讀策書畢，中常侍持皇太子璽綬東向授太子。

translations.literal: When the reading of the edict document is finished, the palace attendant holds the heir apparent's seal-cord and, facing east, hands them to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the patent is read, a palace attendant presents the crown prince's seal and ribbons facing east.

sentences.zh: 太子再拜，三稽首。

translations.literal: The heir apparent twice bows; three times knocks head.
translations.idiomatic: The heir bows twice and performs three forehead knockings.

sentences.zh: 謁者贊皇太子臣某，*

translations.literal: The herald announces 'Heir apparent, subject So-and-so,' *
translations.idiomatic: The herald intones “Heir apparent, your servant So-and-so,”

translations.idiomatic: Some manuscripts insert the placeholder stem 甲 for the personal name.

sentences.zh: **[中]*謁者稱制曰「可」。

translations.literal: The palace herald *[central]* announces by imperial writ: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The chief herald pronounces the edict: Approved.

sentences.zh: 三公升階上殿，賀壽萬歲。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies ascend the steps and enter the hall; they congratulate him on longevity of ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies mount the hall and shout long life to the throne.

sentences.zh: 因大赦天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon there is a great amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign then proclaims a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 供賜禮畢，罷。

translations.literal: When the gifts and grants of the ritual are finished, they dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Once presents are distributed, the assembly disperses.

sentences.zh: 拜諸侯王公之儀：石官會，位定，謁者引光祿勳前。

translations.literal: The ritual for investing feudal kings and dukes: the text reads "officials assemble" (shi guan, stone plus official); when positions are fixed, the herald leads the Superintendent of the Imperial Household forward.

sentences.zh: 腢臣大小鹹以長秋宮未定，遵舊依典，章表仍聞，歷時乃聽。

translations.idiomatic: They cite the vacant Long Autumn halls; petitions echoed until at length they were heard.

translations.idiomatic: This auspicious day elevates Honored Lady Song; she takes her throne on schedule and the realm dances with joy.

sentences.zh: 易稱「受茲介祉」，詩云「干祿百福，子孫千億」，萬方幸甚。

translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi promises great blessing; the Odes prays for countless heirs—the empire shares the joy.

sentences.zh: 今吉日以定，臣請太傅、太尉、司徒、司空、太常條列禮儀正處上，腢臣妾無得上壽，如故事。

translations.literal: Now the auspicious day is fixed; your subjects request the Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, Minister of Works, and Minister of Ceremonies to itemize the ritual procedures and submit them upward; we subjects and concubines may not ascend to offer longevity congratulations, according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They ask the five senior ministers to codify the ceremony and forbid premature longevity toasts from consorts, per precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣囂、臣鼎、臣旭、臣乘、臣滂、臣謨、臣詣愚闇不達大義，誠惶誠恐，頓首死罪，稽首再拜以聞。

translations.literal: Subjects Xiao, Ding, Xu, Cheng, Pang, Mo, and Yi are foolish and dark, not comprehending great righteousness; truly fearful and trembling, knocking head worthy of death, knocking head twice bowing to report.
translations.idiomatic: We are dull and unworthy; trembling, we knock our heads and submit.

translations.idiomatic: Xia, honoring metal, hung reed bundles to symbolize airy interchange.

translations.idiomatic: Shang, with water's virtue, capped gateposts with snail shells to seal damp ingress.

sentences.zh: 周人木德，以桃為更，言氣相更也。

translations.literal: The Zhou people held wood virtue; they used peach for renewal—meaning qi replaces one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, favoring wood, switched to peachwood to mark cyclical renewal.

sentences.zh: 漢兼用之，故以五月五日，朱索五色印為門戶飾，以難止惡氣。

translations.literal: Han combined and used them; therefore on the fifth day of the fifth month, red cords and five-color seals serve as gate and door ornaments, to stop evil qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han blends the customs: on Double Fifth, crimson cords and polychrome charms bar malignant influences.

translations.idiomatic: At the solstice great fires, charcoal works, and saltpetre smelting halt.

translations.idiomatic: Normal industry resumes at Beginning of Autumn.

sentences.zh: 故聖人不取備於一人，必從八能之士。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage does not take completeness in one man; he must follow the eight-power men.
translations.idiomatic: The sage therefore relies on eight specialists, not one all-rounder.

sentences.zh: 故撞鐘者當知鐘，擊鼓者當知鼓，吹管者當知管，吹竿者當知竽，擊磬者當知磬，鼓琴者當知琴。

translations.idiomatic: Each specialist masters one instrument—bell, drum, pipe, yu, chime, and zither.

sentences.zh: 故撞鐘者以知法度，鼓琴者以知四海，擊磬者以知民事。

translations.literal: Therefore he who strikes bells knows law and measure; he who strums se knows the four seas; he who strikes chimes knows the people's tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Bells align statute, zithers read the realm, chimes register popular labor.

sentences.zh: 鐘音調，則君道得；

translations.literal: Bell sound tuned, then lord's way is obtained;
translations.idiomatic: True bell tone means the ruler's path is right;

sentences.zh: 君道得，則黃鐘、蕤賓之律應。

translations.literal: lord's way obtained, then Yellow Bell and Rui Bin pipes respond.
translations.idiomatic: then Yellow Bell and Rui Bin answer in pitch.

sentences.zh: 君道不得，則鐘音不調；

translations.literal: lord's way not obtained, then bell sound not tuned;
translations.idiomatic: a false king mis-tunes the bells;

sentences.zh: 鐘音不調，則黃鐘、蕤賓之律不應。

translations.literal: bell sound not tuned, then Yellow Bell and Rui Bin pipes do not respond.
translations.idiomatic: and those fundamental pipes fall silent.

sentences.zh: 鼓音調，則臣道得；

translations.literal: drum sound tuned, then minister's way is obtained;
translations.idiomatic: True drums show ministers are true;

sentences.zh: 臣道得，則太蔟之律應。

translations.literal: minister's way obtained, then Great Budding pipe responds.
translations.idiomatic: and Great Budding matches them.

sentences.zh: 管音調，則律歷正；

translations.idiomatic: Pipes in tune mark the calendar straight;

sentences.zh: 律歷正，則夷則之律應。

translations.literal: pitch-pipes and calendar correct, then Yi Ze pipe responds.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ze chimes with them.

sentences.zh: 磬音調，則民道得；

translations.literal: chime sound tuned, then people's way is obtained;
translations.idiomatic: Chimes in tune show the people are just;

sentences.zh: 民道得，則林鐘之律應。

translations.literal: people's way obtained, then Forest Bell pipe responds.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell registers the accord.

sentences.zh: 竿音調，則法度得；

translations.literal: yu sound tuned, then law and measure are obtained;
translations.idiomatic: The mouth organ true means laws hold;

sentences.zh: 法度得，則無射之律應。

translations.idiomatic: No Rest answers.

sentences.zh: 琴音調，則四海合歲氣，百川一合德。

sentences.zh: 鬼神之道行，祭祀之道得，如此，則姑洗之律應。

translations.idiomatic: Ghosts and offerings align, and Gu Xi sounds.

sentences.zh: 五樂皆得，則應鐘之律應。

translations.literal: When all five musics are obtained, then Ying Bell pipe responds.
translations.idiomatic: When all five succeed, Ying Bell answers last.

sentences.zh: 天地以和氣至，則和氣應；

sentences.zh: 琴音調，主以德及四海。

translations.literal: Zither sound tuned, lord with virtue reaches to four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Tuned se carries his de to the four seas.

translations.literal: If the text truly meant the Yuanchu period, then Liu Kai would be the one who succeeded Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The chronology implies Liu Kai replaces Xia Qin only under a Yuanchu dating.

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁八行勤*

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 8: “Qin*”
translations.idiomatic: End of a clause naming Xia Qin on folio 3121.

translations.literal: Parenthetical: (and).
translations.idiomatic: Small gloss particle linking clauses.

sentences.zh: **[其]*戒之據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “his admonition to them” for the glossed pronoun—Lu’s reading; agrees with the Comprehensive Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Lu normalizes the pronoun so the emperor’s warning to the ministers is clear.

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁一四行制曰可按：「可」下原衍「之」字，逕刪。

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 14: “The writ says: Approved”—Comment: a spurious zhi after ke was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Editors deleted the stray zhi under “approved.”

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁一四行維建寧四年七月乙未集解引錢大昕說，謂靈帝紀作「七月癸丑」。

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 14: “On the yiwei day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Jianning”—Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling read “seventh month, guichou day.”
translations.idiomatic: Qian notes Lingdi’s annals use a different day stem for the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今按：靈帝建寧四年七月己未朔，無乙未、癸丑。

translations.literal: Verification: in Lingdi’s fourth year of Jianning the seventh month begins on jiwei; neither yiwei nor guichou occurs.
translations.idiomatic: The lunar calendar rules out both stems recorded in the variants.

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁一五行宋貴人*

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 15: “Honored Lady Song*”
translations.idiomatic: Break mid-title for Honored Lady Song.

translations.literal: Gloss: (rides / ascends the carriage).
translations.idiomatic: Alternate wording for the carriage stage direction.

sentences.zh: **[秉]*淑媛之懿據汲本改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “upholding the gentle concubine’s excellence” for the glossed verb—per the Ji manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Ji edition has “grasp, uphold” rather than the erroneous graph.

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁一六行*

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 16: asterisked lacuna.*
translations.idiomatic: A starred break at 3121.16.

translations.literal: Gloss: (person).
translations.idiomatic: Manuscript note supplying ren.

sentences.zh: **[僉]*曰宜哉據汲本改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “All said, ‘How fitting!’” for the glossed adverb—Ji edition; matches the Comprehensive Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: “All” (qian) is the reading Ji and Tongdian share.

sentences.zh: 三一二一頁一六行以*

translations.literal: Folio 3121, line 16: “thereby*”
translations.idiomatic: Clause breaks on yi “thereby.”

translations.literal: Gloss: (oversee).
translations.idiomatic: Variant gloss lin.

sentences.zh: **[母]*兆民據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “to mother the myriad people” or correct homophone “do not harm the myriad people” per context—Lu’s change per Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu aligns the graph with Tongdian’s sense for ruling the people.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁一行今使太尉襲持節奉璽綬按：集解引錢大昕說，謂案靈帝紀，太尉聞人襲以三月免官，此立後乃在七月，或紀所書月日誤。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 1: “We now send Grand Commandant Xi, baton in hand, to present the seal and ribbon”—Comment: Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling show Grand Commandant Wenren Xi dismissed in the third month, whereas this investiture falls in the seventh—perhaps the annals’ month is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian flags a mismatch between the marriage edict and Wenren Xi’s tenure.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁二行太尉住蓋下「住」原斗「注」，逕據汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 2: “The Grand Commandant halts under the canopy”—the graph wrongly written as zhu “pour” was corrected to zhu “stand/stay” per the Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: The archetype miswrote “halt under the canopy”; Ji and Dian restore the standing verb.

sentences.zh: 按：通典作「太尉立階下」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Comprehensive Statutes read “The Grand Commandant stands below the stairs.”
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian imagines him on the steps, not under the canopy.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁三行長*

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 3: “Elder*”
translations.idiomatic: Fragment ending in zhang “elder / senior.”

translations.literal: Gloss: (music).
translations.idiomatic: Alternate reading yue “music.”

sentences.zh: **[秋]*太僕據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “Grand Coachman of Autumn” for the glossed season—Lu’s correction.
translations.idiomatic: Lu gives the autumn coachman, not the music office.

sentences.zh: 按：盧雲通典「樂」作「秋」，是。

translations.literal: Comment: Lu says Tongdian writes “autumn” where this text has “music”; that is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The seasonal title fits the autumn hunt context.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁六行彌牟*[樸]*蠱鐘據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 6: “Mi Mou’s *[simple]* gu bells”—pu “simple” supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Editors restore the description of the ritual bells.

sentences.zh: 按：集解引錢大昕說，謂彌牟五字未詳。

translations.literal: Comment: Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the five characters “Mi Mou…” remain unexplained.
translations.idiomatic: Qian admits the phrase is obscure.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁七行以桃印長六寸方三寸按：盧雲宋志「印」作「卯」。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 7: “Using a peach talisman six cun long and three cun square”—Comment: Lu says the Song Treatise writes mao peg where this has seal yin.
translations.idiomatic: Song texts speak of a peach peg, not a seal.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁八行慎其閉塞按：「塞」原斗「寒」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 8: “Guard against blockage”—Comment: “block” sai was miswritten as “cold” han; corrected.
translations.idiomatic: A simple homophone fix for sai.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁一０行消石冶皆絕止按：「冶」原斗「治」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 10: “Saltpeter and smelting all cease”—Comment: “smelt” ye was miswritten as “govern” zhi; corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The edition restores ye “smelting works.”

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁一一行*[湯]*始得伊尹據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 11: “*[Tang]* first obtained Yi Yin”—Tang supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian supply the founder Cheng Tang.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁一二行誰能出不由戶*

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 12: “Who can leave without using the door*”
translations.idiomatic: Half-line quoting the adage about doors.

translations.literal: Particle gloss: (the one who…).
translations.idiomatic: Optional classical particle zhe.

sentences.zh: *據汲本、殿本刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete the marked syllable per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian drop the extra character.

sentences.zh: 三一二二頁一二行欲人之子孫蕃*

translations.literal: Folio 3122, line 12: “Desiring that people’s descendants multiply*”
translations.idiomatic: Line on abundant posterity.

translations.literal: Gloss: (plant).
translations.idiomatic: Graph zhi “plant.”

sentences.zh: **[殖]*據殿本改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “multiply” zhi for the glossed graph—Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition uses the character for proliferation, not planting.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁三行迎氣*[於]*白郊據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 3: “Welcoming the qi *[at]* the white suburb”—yi “at” supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Editors add yi before “white suburb.”

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁五行立秋之日*

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 5: “On the day Beginning of Autumn*”
translations.idiomatic: Date formula interrupted.

translations.literal: Gloss: (from).
translations.idiomatic: Particle zi “from.”

sentences.zh: **[白]*郊禮畢據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “When the white-suburb rite ends” for the glossed color word—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu specifies the white-suburb sequence.

sentences.zh: 按：盧雲通典同，今從宋志。

translations.literal: Comment: Lu says the Comprehensive Statutes agree; this edition follows the Song Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The editors prefer Song Treatise wording over other witnesses.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁六行載*[以]*獲車馳*

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 6: “Load *[with]* the catch-cart galloping*”
translations.idiomatic: Fragment about the game cart.

translations.literal: Gloss: (four-horse team).
translations.idiomatic: Note on si “four-in-hand.”

sentences.zh: *送陵廟據盧校補刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: supplement and delete so the line reads “sent to the mausoleum shrines”—per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu both adds and trims to match the ritual route.

sentences.zh: 按：盧雲通典有「以」字，此脫。

translations.literal: Comment: Lu says Tongdian has the word yi “with”; it fell out here.
translations.idiomatic: The preposition yi is missing in this witness.

sentences.zh: 「駟」字衍，宋志無。

translations.literal: The character si “four-horse” is redundant; the Song Treatise omits it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Treatise drops si.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁七行*[於是乘輿]*還宮據集解引惠棟說補。

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 7: *[“Thereupon the imperial carriage”]* returns to the palace—supplemented per Collected glosses citing Hui Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong’s conjecture restores the carriage sentence.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁九行烹鮮時有司*[告]*據盧校改。

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 9: “When the fresh meat is cooked, the officials *[announce]*”—gai “announce” per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu reads the verb as “announce,” not a near homophone.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁一０行天子乃厲*

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 10: “The Son of Heaven then tempers*”
translations.idiomatic: Ritual line about the emperor preparing.

translations.literal: Manuscript lacuna mark (square).
translations.idiomatic: The block marks unreadable text.

sentences.zh: **[飾]*盧云「□」當作「飾」，月令正義雲俗本作「飭」，此又轉鬥。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “adorn” shi—Lu says the lacuna should be shi; the Monthly Ordinances commentary notes vulgar editions use chi “order,” which itself miscopied again here.
translations.idiomatic: Lu restores shi; the corruption chain runs lacuna ← chi ← shi.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: The text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors adopt Lu’s shi.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁一０行所以教兆民*

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 10: “The means by which to instruct the myriad people*”
translations.idiomatic: Clause on instructing the populace.

translations.literal: Gloss: (record / convey).
translations.idiomatic: Variant zai “carry, record.”

sentences.zh: *戰事也據盧校刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete “it is a military matter” per Lu’s edition.
translations.idiomatic: Lu removes the martial gloss.

sentences.zh: 三一二三頁一三行引*

translations.literal: Folio 3123, line 13: “Lead*”
translations.idiomatic: Verb yin “draw, lead.”

translations.literal: Gloss: (threshold).
translations.idiomatic: Note on yu “threshold.”

sentences.zh: **[關]*蹋踘之屬也據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “barrier games such as cuju” for the glossed graph—Lu’s edition.
translations.idiomatic: Lu interprets the word as guan “bar, bolt,” i.e. sports.

sentences.zh: 三一二四頁四行巡狩*[校]*獵還據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3124, line 4: “After the royal tour and *[inspection]* hunt return”—“inspect” xiao supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian insert xiao before the hunt.

sentences.zh: 三一二四頁五行公卿*[親]*識顏色據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3124, line 5: “The dukes and ministers *[in person]* observe his complexion”—qin “personally” supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian stress personal scrutiny by the lords.

sentences.zh: 三一二四頁一０行膢臘而寘水按：校補謂今風俗通「寘」作「買」，今韓非子「寘水」作「相遺以水」。

translations.literal: Folio 3124, line 10: “Lu month end-offering and placing water”—Comment: Collators say the current Fengsu tong writes “buy” for “place”; the current Han Feizi has “present water to one another” instead of “place water.”
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts disagree on zhi “place” versus commerce or gift.

sentences.zh: 三一二四頁一一行又曰*

translations.literal: Folio 3124, line 11: “It also says*”
translations.idiomatic: Introductory formula mid-page.

translations.literal: Gloss: (ought).
translations.idiomatic: Particle dang.

sentences.zh: **[嘗]*新始殺*[也]*食*[新]*曰貙膢據盧校刪補，與今風俗通合。

translations.literal: Emendation: “Tasting the new, first kill *[particle]*; eating the new is called the autumn lu sacrifice”—deleted and supplied per Lu; matches the current Fengsu tong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s patch aligns with Fengsu tong’s wording for the harvest tasting.

sentences.zh: 三一二四頁一三行王杖長*[九]*尺據盧校補。

translations.literal: Folio 3124, line 13: “The king’s staff measures *[nine]* chi long”—“nine” supplied per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu adds the length nine chi from other witnesses.

sentences.zh: 按：盧雲據御覽七百十補。

translations.literal: Comment: Lu says it is supplemented from the Imperial Readings, scroll 710.
translations.idiomatic: The number comes from Yulan 710.

sentences.zh: 三一二五頁一二行*

translations.literal: Folio 3125, line 12: asterisk break.*
translations.idiomatic: Starred lacuna on folio 3125.

translations.literal: Gloss: (gentleman of the palace).
translations.idiomatic: Note lang “court gentleman.”

sentences.zh: **[即]*坐於端門左塾據汲本改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “they immediately sit in the left schoolroom of the Zhu Gate”—Ji edition.
translations.idiomatic: Ji edition uses ji “immediately,” not lang.

sentences.zh: 三一二五頁一二行*

translations.literal: Folio 3125, line 12: asterisk break.*
translations.idiomatic: Second starred break on the same folio line.

sentences.zh: (太子)

translations.literal: Gloss: (crown prince).
translations.idiomatic: Words taizi supplied as variant.

sentences.zh: **[大予]*具樂器據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “Grand Presenter” preparer of instruments—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu restores the Grand Presenter bandmaster title.

sentences.zh: 按：集解引錢大昕說，謂「太子」當作「大予」，又引惠棟說，謂當作「太常」。

translations.literal: Comment: Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: “crown prince” should be “Grand Presenter”; Hui Dong adds it might instead read “Minister of Ceremonies.”
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Hui propose different offices for the musician heading.

sentences.zh: 觀下文引蔡邕禮樂志，漢樂四品，一曰大予樂，則錢說是。

translations.literal: Considering the passage below quoting Cai Yong’s Treatise on Rites and Music—Han music in four grades, the first called Grand Presenter music—Qian’s identification is right.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong’s fourfold scheme confirms “Grand Presenter,” not the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁五行皆音以竽按：集解引黃山說，謂此承上「閒音以竽」言，「皆」下當脫「閒」字。

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 5: “All take their pitch from the yu-pipes”—Comment: Collected glosses cite Huang Shan: this continues the earlier line “interpolate pitch with yu”; after “all” the word “interpolate” is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang argues jian dropped out after jie “all.”

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁七行否則召太史令各板書按：校補引錢大昭說，謂「板書」閩本作「書板」。

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 7: “Otherwise summon the Grand Astrologer, each to write on boards”—Comment: Collators cite Qian Dazhao: Fujian editions reverse the compound to “write boards.”
translations.idiomatic: Board-write versus write-board is a word-order variant.

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁八行施當軒北面稽首按：盧云「施」疑「旋」之鬥。

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 8: “Spreading at the casement, facing north, he knocks his head”—Comment: Lu suspects shi is a miswriting of xuan “turn.”
translations.idiomatic: Lu prefers “turn at the casement” to “spread.”

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁九行太史令前*

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 9: “The Grand Astrologer steps forward*”
translations.idiomatic: Incomplete clause on the astrologer advancing.

translations.literal: Gloss: (says).
translations.idiomatic: Speech marker yue.

sentences.zh: **[白]*禮畢據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read “reports: the rite is finished” for the glossed verb—Lu’s edition.
translations.idiomatic: Lu uses bai “report,” not a near homophone.

sentences.zh: 按：集解引惠棟說，謂北宋本作「白」。

translations.literal: Comment: Collected glosses cite Hui Dong: Northern Song editions have bai.
translations.idiomatic: Early printings agree on bai.

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁一二行故八士*

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 12: “Therefore the eight masters*”
translations.idiomatic: Opening of a quotation about the eight worthies.

translations.literal: Gloss: (say).
translations.idiomatic: Speech marker yue closing the gloss block.

sentences.zh: *或調陰陽據盧校刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete ‘or harmonize yin and yang’ per Lu Wenchao’s edition.
translations.idiomatic: Lu’s text drops the phrase about adjusting yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 三一二六頁一六行琴音調則四海合歲氣百川一合德按：盧云「一」或作「以」。

translations.literal: Folio 3126, line 16: ‘When the qin’s pitch is tuned, the four seas harmonize; the year’s qi and the hundred streams unite in virtue’—Comment: Lu says ‘one’ might alternately be read as yi ‘by means of.’
translations.idiomatic: Lu allows yi instead of ‘one’ in the cosmic harmony line.

sentences.zh: 三一二七頁四行迎送*

translations.literal: Folio 3127, line 4: ‘welcoming and sending off*’
translations.idiomatic: Fragment about welcoming and escorting parties.

sentences.zh: (凡田獵)

translations.literal: Stage direction: (whenever hunting).
translations.idiomatic: Rubric: applies generally to the hunt.

sentences.zh: **[五日臘]*者歲終大祭據殿本改，與盧校本獨斷合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘the fifth day’s la sacrifice’ for the wax-day formula—Palace edition; matches Lu’s Duanguan recension alone.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and Lu’s Duanguan agree on the fifth-day year-end offering.

sentences.zh: 三一二七頁八行秦靜曰按：「秦」原斗「泰」，逕改正。

translations.literal: Folio 3127, line 8: ‘Qin Jing says’—Comment: ‘Qin’ was miswritten as ‘great peace’ Thai; corrected outright.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator’s surname is Qin, not Tai.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁四行司馬闕門門外按：集解引黃山說，謂秦蕙田據舊本，「門外」作「之外」。

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 4: ‘The marshal leaves the gate outside the gate’—Comment: Collected glosses cite Huang Shan: Qin Huitian’s old edition reads ‘beyond’ for ‘outside.’
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses disagree on whether the clause repeats ‘gate’ or uses ‘beyond.’

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁五行郁櫑汲本、殿本「櫑」作「儡」，注同。

translations.literal: Yu lei—Ji and Palace editions write the second character as puppet lei; commentary matches.
translations.idiomatic: Prints vary between lei ‘stack’ and homophones in the torch-bearing passage.

sentences.zh: 文選東京賦作「壘」。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital rhapsody in the Wen xuan writes ‘rampart.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng’s poem prefers the fortification graph.

sentences.zh: 按：郁儡之「儡」或作「壘」，無作「櫑」者，疑此誤。

translations.literal: Comment: for ‘dim stacks’ the second character may be puppet or rampart, never ‘stacked shelves’; this print is probably wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Editors suspect this witness misread the rare lei graphs.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁八行是為*

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 8: ‘This is called*’
translations.idiomatic: Formula introducing a demon’s name.

translations.literal: Gloss: (tiger).
translations.idiomatic: Manuscript note hu ‘tiger.’

sentences.zh: **[虐鬼]*據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘cruel demon’ or ‘malaria demon’ for the glossed phrase—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu restores the plague-demon wording.

sentences.zh: 按：虐即瘧字，虎與虐形近而鬥。

translations.literal: Comment: cruel is the malaria graph; tiger and cruel look alike and were confused.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger demon arose from a graphic slip for malaria.

sentences.zh: 文選東京賦注正作「瘧鬼」。

translations.literal: The Wen xuan commentary on the Eastern Capital rhapsody correctly writes ‘malaria demon.’
translations.idiomatic: The received commentary has ‘malaria ghost.’

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁八行一居人宮室區隅*

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 8: ‘One lodges in the corner of a human dwelling*’
translations.idiomatic: Line about a specter in house corners.

sentences.zh: (漚庾)

translations.literal: Gloss: (ouyu—a phonetic gloss).
translations.idiomatic: Interlinear note ouyu for ‘corner.’

sentences.zh: *按：文選東京賦注無「漚庾」二字，當即「區隅」之音注，而誤入正文者，今刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: the Wen xuan commentary lacks the two characters ouyu; they are only a pronunciation gloss on ‘corner’ that slipped into the main text—delete.
translations.idiomatic: Editors remove intrusive phonetic characters.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁一一行方相帥百隸及童*

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 11: ‘The leizi commander leads a hundred underlings and boys and girls*’
translations.idiomatic: Processional line about the exorcist chief.

translations.literal: Gloss: (female).
translations.idiomatic: Note nü ‘female’ rather than generic children.

sentences.zh: **[子]*據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘children’ zi—Lu’s edition.
translations.idiomatic: Lu specifies boys and girls as zi.

sentences.zh: 按：文選注作「子」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Wen xuan commentary writes zi.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel commentary agrees on zi.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁一三行*

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 13: asterisk break.*
translations.idiomatic: Starred lacuna mid-line on folio 3128.

translations.literal: Gloss: (discard).
translations.idiomatic: Variant graph juan ‘cast aside.’

sentences.zh: **[捎]*魑魅據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘brush aside’ shao the mountain sprites—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu uses shao ‘sweep away’ for driving off chimei.

sentences.zh: 按：文選注作「捎」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Wen xuan commentary writes shao.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel gloss agrees with shao.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁一六行*

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 16: asterisk break.*
translations.idiomatic: Second starred break on the folio.

translations.literal: Gloss: (subject / minister).
translations.idiomatic: Note chen where another witness differs.

sentences.zh: **[韋]*昭曰木石*[謂]*山*[怪]*也據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: ‘Wei Zhao says: “Trees and rocks *[mean]* mountain *[sprites]*”’—edited per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu restores Wei Zhao’s gloss on mountain monsters.

sentences.zh: 按：此劉昭引韋昭注國語文，「臣」當作「韋」。

translations.literal: Comment: here Liu Zhao cites Wei Zhao’s Guoyu commentary; chen should be Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The surname was miscopied as chen ‘minister.’

sentences.zh: 「木石山怪也」今國語韋昭注作「木石謂山也」，盧依韋注改。

translations.literal: ‘Trees and rocks are mountains’ in today’s Guoyu Wei commentary—Lu follows Wei and revises accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu aligns the quotation with the Guoyu commentary.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁一六行越人謂*[之]*山□據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 16: ‘The Yue people call them *[it]* mountain [lacuna]’—zhi ‘them’ supplied per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian add the object pronoun before the mountain name.

sentences.zh: 按：「□」今國語韋注作「繅」。

translations.literal: Comment: the lacuna in today’s Guoyu Wei commentary reads sao ‘reel silk.’
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao’s text fills the gap with the graph sao.

sentences.zh: 三一二八頁一六行好學人聲按：今國語韋注「學」作「□」。

translations.literal: Folio 3128, line 16: ‘Fond of mimicking human voices’—Comment: in today’s Guoyu Wei commentary ‘study’ is a lacuna mark.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel text leaves xue unreadable or omitted.

sentences.zh: 三一二九頁一行一名沐□按：汲本、殿本「□」作「□」，盧文弨依國語韋注改為「腫」。

translations.literal: Folio 3129, line 1: ‘First name Mu[lacuna]’—Comment: Ji and Palace editions show a lacuna for another lacuna; Lu Wencha follows the Guoyu Wei commentary in reading zhong ‘swelling demon.’
translations.idiomatic: Lu resolves the corrupted demon name using Wei Zhao.

sentences.zh: 三一二九頁一二行尚書令各五千按：盧云「令」下疑脫「史」字。

translations.literal: Folio 3129, line 12: ‘Each Minister of Education receives five thousand’—Comment: Lu suspects the word shi ‘clerk’ dropped after ‘minister.’
translations.idiomatic: Lu would supply clerks under each minister.

sentences.zh: 三一二九頁一三行以為當祠門戶直按：「噹」原斗「富」，逕據汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Folio 3129, line 13: ‘Therefore proper sacrifice at household gates’—Comment: ‘watchman’s bell’ dang was miswritten as ‘wealth’ fu; corrected per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian restore dang for gate vigil.

sentences.zh: 三一二九頁一五行是月之*

translations.literal: Folio 3129, line 15: ‘In that month’s*’
translations.idiomatic: Month formula interrupted.

translations.literal: Gloss: (assembly).
translations.idiomatic: Variant hui ‘gathering.’

sentences.zh: **[昏]*建丑據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘dusk sets the chou hour’—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu sets the evening asterism line.

sentences.zh: 三一三０頁四行周禮*

translations.literal: Folio 3130, line 4: ‘The Rites of Zhou*’
translations.idiomatic: Citation of Zhou li opening.

translations.literal: Gloss: (says).
translations.idiomatic: Speech marker yue.

sentences.zh: *府史以下據盧校刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete ‘clerks below the bureau chiefs’ per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu removes the Zhou li gloss about subclerks.

sentences.zh: 三一三０頁六行每*

translations.literal: Folio 3130, line 6: ‘Each*’
translations.idiomatic: Sentence fragment on ‘each.’

sentences.zh: (月朔)

translations.literal: Gloss: (new-moon of the month).
translations.idiomatic: Words yue shuo supplied.

sentences.zh: *歲首*[正月]*據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: ‘year’s beginning *[first month]*’—Lu’s revision.
translations.idiomatic: Lu clarifies the New Year court.

sentences.zh: 按：盧云「每月朔歲首」鬥，今從通典。

translations.literal: Comment: Lu says ‘each month’s new moon’ and ‘year’s beginning’ were conflated; this edition follows the Comprehensive Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian keeps the phrases distinct.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁一行百官各陪*[位]*朝賀據盧校補，與通典合。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 1: ‘Every office attends court-in-audience, each taking his *[station]*’—wei ‘position’ supplied per Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu inserts wei so officials stand in rank.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁二行皆*[陛]*覲據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 2: ‘All *[mount the stairs for]* audience’—supplemented per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian add the verb for ascending to audience.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁二行宗室諸劉*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 2: ‘Imperial Liu clansmen*’
translations.idiomatic: Line on imperial surname nobles.

translations.literal: Gloss: (mixed).
translations.idiomatic: Note za ‘mixed’ attendance.

sentences.zh: **[親]*會萬人以上據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘kinsmen assemble, more than ten thousand’—Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian reads qin for kin gathering.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁二行位*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 2: ‘Positions*’
translations.idiomatic: Fragment on seating.

sentences.zh: (公納薦太官賜食酒西入東出)

translations.literal: Stage direction: (dukes present viands; the Minister of Royal Household grants food and wine; enter from the west, exit east).
translations.idiomatic: Long rubric for banquet movement.

sentences.zh: *既定據盧校刪，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete ‘once settled’ per Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu drops the redundant ‘already settled’ clause.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁三行*[腢]*計吏中庭北面立據盧校補。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 3: ‘*[Commandery]* clerks for the census stand in the courtyard facing north’—supplemented per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu supplies the graph for district clerks at court.

sentences.zh: 按：通典無「立」字。

translations.literal: Comment: Tongdian lacks the verb ‘stand.’
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian omits li ‘stand.’

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁三行太官上食賜腢臣酒食*[西入東出]*據盧校補。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 3: ‘The Minister of Royal Household serves food and grants wine and viands to the clerks *[enter west, exit east]*’—supplemented per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu adds the circuit around the hall.

sentences.zh: 按：通典作「太官賜酒食，西入東出」。

translations.literal: Comment: Tongdian reads ‘Minister grants wine and food; enter west, exit east.’
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian splits the sentence slightly differently.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁三行*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 3: asterisk break.*
translations.idiomatic: Starred lacuna before the censors.

sentences.zh: (貢事)

translations.literal: Gloss: (tribute business).
translations.idiomatic: Phrase gong shi ‘reporting tribute.’

sentences.zh: *御史四人執法殿下據盧校刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: delete ‘four law-enforcing censors below the hall’ per Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu removes the censor clause.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁三行虎賁羽林*[張]**

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 3: ‘Tiger guards and feathered forest archers *[miswritten zhang]* **’
translations.idiomatic: Line on guards with an erroneous character marked for emendation.

translations.literal: Gloss: (bow).
translations.idiomatic: Correct graph hu ‘bow.’

translations.literal: Fragment: ‘*bow*’
translations.idiomatic: The word gong ‘bow’ restored.

translations.literal: Gloss: (nock / pinch).
translations.idiomatic: Note cuo ‘nock’ or related.

sentences.zh: **[挾]*矢據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘clutch arrows’ xie—Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian and Lu agree on xie for tucked arrows.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁四行左右中郎將*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 4: ‘Left and right commandants of the Gentleman-of-the-Household cadres*’
translations.idiomatic: Line on zhonglang generals.

translations.literal: Gloss: (station / halt).
translations.idiomatic: Variant zhu ‘post.’

translations.literal: Emendation: ‘*[take]* station east*’
translations.idiomatic: Lu begins the compass directions.

translations.literal: Gloss: (west).
translations.idiomatic: Direction xi.

sentences.zh: **[南]*據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘south’—Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu completes the arc as south; Tongdian agrees.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁五行作九賓*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 5: ‘Perform the nine-guest protocol*’
translations.idiomatic: State ritual with nine guests.

translations.literal: Gloss: (withdraw).
translations.idiomatic: Stage marker che ‘pull away.’

sentences.zh: **[散]*樂據盧校改，與通典合。

translations.literal: Emendation: read ‘dismiss the music’ san—Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Closing fanfare uses san ‘scatter’ music.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁五行捨利*[獸]*從西方來據盧校補，與通典合。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 5: ‘Sheli tribute beasts come from the west’—beasts supplied per Lu; matches Tongdian. (Sheli: transliteration of the foreign animal act.)
translations.idiomatic: Lu adds the Western animal pageant; ‘Sheli’ transliterates the name in the source.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁六行以兩大絲繩系兩柱*

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 6: ‘Two great silk ropes tie the two pillars*’
translations.idiomatic: Acrobatic rigging description.

sentences.zh: (中頭)

translations.literal: Gloss: (between the capitals / mid-span).
translations.idiomatic: Note zhong tou ‘between tops.’

sentences.zh: *閒按：通典作「又以絲繩系兩柱閒」，無「中頭」二字，今據刪。

translations.literal: Emendation: Tongdian reads ‘Further tie silk ropes between the two pillars’ without the two characters ‘mid-span’—delete per Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Editors drop zhong tou to match Tongdian.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁七行*[倡]*樂畢作魚龍曼延據盧校補，與通典合。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 7: ‘*[Variety]* music ends; perform fish-dragon pageantry’—supplemented per Lu; matches Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu supplies chang ‘variety entertainment’ before the fish-dragon show.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁八行陛高二丈按：通典「二丈」作「一丈」。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 8: ‘The steps are two zhang high’—Comment: Tongdian reads ‘one zhang.’
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian halves the stair height.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁九行激沼水於殿下按：盧雲此六字衍，通典無。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 9: ‘Surging pond water below the hall’—Comment: Lu says these six characters are intrusive; Tongdian lacks them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu deletes the pumped-water gloss.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁九行玉階金柱按：通典「階」作「陛」。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 9: ‘Jade stairs, gold pillars’—Comment: Tongdian writes ‘terraces’ for ‘stairs.’
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian prefers jade terrace.

sentences.zh: 三一三一頁一七行*[詩]*所謂琴瑟擊鼓據殿本補。

translations.literal: Folio 3131, line 17: ‘What the *[Odes]* call “strike zithers and se, beat drums”’—supplemented per Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition cites the Poetry tag.

sentences.zh: 三一三二頁二行王*[師]*大*

translations.literal: Folio 3132, line 2: ‘The king *[shi]* great*’
translations.idiomatic: Fragment of the Zhou li quotation on victory music.

translations.literal: Gloss: (victory / triumph).
translations.idiomatic: Note jie ‘triumph.’

sentences.zh: **[獻]*則令凱樂據盧校改。

translations.literal: Emendation: ‘when *[offerings]* are presented, then order triumphal music’—Lu’s text.
translations.idiomatic: Lu uses xian for presenting spoils before the triumph tune.

sentences.zh: 按：周禮「令」下有「奏」字。

translations.literal: Comment: the Rites of Zhou inserts zou ‘perform’ after ‘order.’
translations.idiomatic: The canonical Zhou li adds zou before the music command.
